problems: There is no stone anywhere in the picture. The 'magnet stone' is a flat black ellipse that looks like a hole in the sand (every storyboard frame and the 25/50/75 stills), so a viewer reads it as a putting hole, not a sunken magnet.
The balls start moving on their own. They sit in the top-left corner (frame 1) and set off one by one (frames 2 and 7) with no putt, push or visible slope to start them.

The 'one goes straight' ball crosses the tray diagonally and stops dead in the middle of open sand (frames 3-5, 25% still). It hits nothing and nothing stops it, and the tray looks flat, so 'roll down' isn't readable.

The 'one swings round it' claim isn't shown. The second ball passes above the dark ellipse and stops in open sand above the first ball (frames 7-9, 50% still). At this distance and frame spacing no curve around the stone can be seen, so it looks like another straight roll that stopped short.

The 'one stops on it' ball ends half inside the black ellipse, dark against dark and partly cut off by its rim (frames 13-16, 75% still). It reads as a ball dropping into a hole, and it's hard to see.
The tray's near rail is broken. One front plank lies loose and slanted on the grass, apart from the rest of the frame, leaving a gap in the border (all frames).
Half the tray, including the stone and two ball paths, sits in a big soft shadow, and the balls are tiny dark dots against it (frames 2, 7, 11-12).
The last quarter of the film is frozen: frames 13-16 show nothing moving for about 2 s.
posts.critique: The caption promises three different behaviours around a magnet stone, but the film shows three tiny balls that start rolling with nothing pushing them, stop in empty sand and drop into a black hole, with no stone in sight. The broken front rail and the heavy shadow over the action make it worse.
